questions.passage: Despite all the criticisms, Allport and Odbert’s early effort to catalog personality trait words has survived as the “lexical approach” to personality.
questions.prompt: What does “Despite all the criticisms” highlight?
options: The early effort remained influential as the lexical approach even though it was criticised.
Every criticism was disproved and the original list was left unchanged forever.
The lexical approach was abandoned immediately.
Personality research stopped using language in any form.
questions.promptZh: Despite all the criticisms 强调什么？
optionsZh: 尽管受批评，早期工作仍以词汇取向延续并保持影响。
所有批评均被推翻，原名单永远不变。
词汇取向立即被抛弃。
人格研究停止使用任何语言材料。
analyses: A despite 引出让步，has survived 表明方法传统延续。
B 延续不等于每条批评无效，也不保证原始词表不变。
C 与 has survived 相反。
D lexical approach 本身就是从词汇研究人格的取向。

evidence.quote: Allport and Odbert’s early effort to catalog personality trait words has survived as the “lexical approach” to personality.

vocabulary.context: 通过人格描述词研究特质的取向，不是把每个词都当作独立维度
vocabulary.example: The seminar introduced the lexical approach to personality.

questions.prompt: How did the psychologists organise the personality terms into broader factors?

They collected self-ratings and used factor analysis to group the terms.

questions.promptZh: 心理学家怎样把人格词汇整理为更宽泛的因子？
optionsZh: 让评分者不经统计分析选出最熟悉的五个词。
收集自我评分，再用因素分析把词汇归组。

把所有自评换成对学生父母的观察。
analyses: A 原文明确用了 factor analysis，非仅凭熟悉度选择。

D themselves 表示自评，没有父母观察这一程序。

evidence.quote: rate themselves using many of the original Allport-Odbert terms, then applied the statistical technique of factor analysis

vocabulary.context: 把许多词条的评分整理为较大组的统计方法，不是按人数命名人格类型

questions.passage: The more new conversations you enter, the psychologically richer the party becomes for you. Someone who has a psychologically enriching experience at one party is more likely to go to another party.

B 将 more new conversations 的方向倒置，还添加 always。

is more likely to go to another party.

questions.passage: It is interesting to note that Greta Thunberg appears more neurotic than most. She worries intensely about environmental disasters and climate change. However, she seems to leverage her anxiety to fuel her work. So long as one’s neuroticism is not overwhelming, a meaningful life is possible.
questions.prompt: Which reading best respects the caution in the author’s description of Thunberg?
options: The author suggests anxiety may fuel her work, without presenting a clinical diagnosis.
The author reports a medical test proving that anxiety always improves performance.
The passage says that a meaningful life requires overwhelming anxiety.
The passage establishes that she never worries about environmental problems.
questions.promptZh: 哪种理解最保留作者描述 Thunberg 时的谨慎语气？
optionsZh: 作者认为焦虑可能推动她的工作，并未呈现临床诊断。
作者报告医学检测，证明焦虑总能提高表现。
有意义人生必须具有压倒性的焦虑。
书中确立她从不担忧环境问题。
analyses: A appears、seems 均保留观察与解释的不确定性，本段没有临床测量。
B 没有医学检测，也无 always 的普遍保证。
C not overwhelming 才是最后一句的条件，不能删掉 not。
D worries intensely 明确相反；人格术语不应直接替换成对人物的疾病诊断。

evidence.quote: she seems to leverage her anxiety to fuel her work.
So long as one’s neuroticism is not overwhelming, a meaningful life is possible.

vocabulary.context: 动词，比喻焦虑成为工作动力；作者使用 seems 保留推测
vocabulary.example: Her curiosity helped fuel a long research project.

questions.translation: 值得注意的是，Thunberg 似乎比多数人更具神经质倾向。她强烈担忧环境灾难和气候变化。然而，她似乎把焦虑转化为工作的动力。只要神经质倾向没有强到令人无法承受，有意义的人生仍然可能。
